objective_record.compatibility: a legacy suite record (version 2) without the section and a version-4 record without the identity both still verify, which is what keeps the runs of this experiment written by both writers valid; the current version's writer always emits both, so deleting either from a newly written record is reported. A record whose configuration has no Tetris agent must not carry the section, because no writer emits one.

identity.covers: the declaring module and the modules its code calls — the frozen geometry and board model it imports and Experiment 002's reachable-set enumeration it reuses — discovered from the objective's own namespace rather than hand-listed, so a module that stops being used drops out of the identity by itself and a helper cannot change the objective's values unrecorded
identity.gating: required at version 5, the version this repair writes; optional at version 4 and 2, whose writers recorded no identity, and compared when present
identity.value: one sha256 per package module the objective's decisions are computed from, keyed by module name
identity.why: the weights are constants, so a formula change that leaves them alone changes every value the objective computes while the recorded weights still compare equal, and the replayed choices catch it only when the change happens to move one of them. The reviewer's counterexample — the clear term charging a premature clear at twice the declared rate — keeps every weight and is reported by this identity alone

objective_record.place: a top-level suite section beside the frozen heuristic mapping, never a leaf inside an episode or its result; required by a suite that uses the Tetris agent at every version whose writer emits one (4 and 5), optional only at the legacy version 2
objective_record.source: tetris.weights_record(): the declared weights, the well-depth cap and the tie-break rule, plus the objective's source identity
objective_record.verification: verify_run compares the recorded module name, weights and source identity with the current module's under the same exact type-and-key rules it applies to the heuristic mapping, so a suite that uses the Tetris agent cannot verify under a different objective merely because the change preserved its replayed choices; live play, the second path that writes suite records, records the same section for a live Tetris game
objective_record.why: the frozen heuristic mapping is recorded for every suite because every placement agent scores through it, and the Tetris agent's choices come from a second, separately declared objective; before this section existed a suite record was tied to its objective only through the replayed choices, so a changed objective still verified whenever the change happened to preserve them, and before the identity existed a changed formula still verified whenever its weights were unchanged

predeclared_objective.note: the capture records the module digest and the digest of the notes' declared-objective section — the weights table and rationale alone, delimited by the predeclared-objective markers — and is not overwritten while both still match; the cited record was created after this capture, which check-predeclaration re-checks mechanically. The capture was re-made three times as the marked section changed; the final text is the objective alone (the provenance and replay-guarantee note now sits below the end marker), and the superseded captures are kept beside it

objective.tie_break: first highest-valued placement in canonical enumeration order: orientation ascending, then column ascending

publication.compared_paths: every path either tree tracks, plus this worktree's untracked files, derived from Git: a declared list can omit a path the task changes, and the review found that hole twice (first this record's own result.json, then any tracked path outside the list); 46 paths in the published tree at this round's run
publication.note: publication is service-owned and gated on an exact-tree approval, so the branch ref and the PR head move together: the probe asserts that the two refs name one commit and that the commit descends from the recorded base, and it compares the compared paths' content — per-file sha256 in the published clone beside this worktree's — instead of their presence. When the contents differ it requires the difference to be exactly the repair this worktree holds uncommitted, prints the differing paths and reports the earlier-publication state instead of calling the repair published; a published tree differing from a clean worktree fails. Every field above is read from the single run whose command and capture time are recorded here, and the run's own two emitted lines are quoted rather than paraphrased: `state` is its state line verbatim and `counts_line` is its counts line verbatim (declared_paths_compared_by_content / compared_paths_count / observed_differing_paths / observed_uncommitted_paths). `evidence.py publication-record` reconstructs the state line from the record's own commit, compared-path count and differing-path list and requires it to be `state`, requires the declared count to be the declared list's own length, and requires `counts_line` to be the probe's own counts line for the fields beside it, so the two lines, the counts and the commit fields have to be one run's
publication.repaired_paths: the 12 files this experiment adds or repairs: the runner's metric and objective identity, the live path that records them, the agents module, the Tetris objective, this record and the notes, both probes, the experiments index and the two suites and the live suite (src/block_stack_ai/runner.py, src/block_stack_ai/live.py, src/block_stack_ai/agents.py, src/block_stack_ai/tetris.py, experiments/003-tetris-aware-agent/notes.md, experiments/003-tetris-aware-agent/result.json, experiments/003-tetris-aware-agent/probes/evidence.py, experiments/003-tetris-aware-agent/probes/prechange_probe.py, experiments/README.md, tests/test_unit.py, tests/test_integration.py, tests/test_live.py); compared per file by sha256, since presence cannot tell a published repair from an earlier publication containing the same names. `repaired_paths_compared_by_content` is not transcribed: it is the `declared_paths_compared_by_content` value of the run's own counts line, cited verbatim in counts_line, and `publication-record` requires it to be this list's own length — the earlier record said 11 while experiments/README.md made the declaration 12. This record is in the list: the review found it missing, so a state where every other compared path matched but the reported result was still the previous round's would have been certified as published
publication.state: the refs name an earlier publication: ed8830a15d05a70fbd1783e4a6faa26df78a1d05; 9 of 46 compared paths differ from this worktree (experiments/003-tetris-aware-agent/notes.md, experiments/003-tetris-aware-agent/probes/evidence.py, experiments/003-tetris-aware-agent/probes/prechange_probe.py, experiments/003-tetris-aware-agent/result.json, experiments/README.md, src/block_stack_ai/runner.py, tests/test_integration.py, tests/test_live.py, tests/test_unit.py), and this worktree holds the unpublished repair
publication.states: each compared path's state is read once per side — a file with its sha256, a directory, or absent — and reported in one of the states a comparison has: identical, differing, deleted from this worktree while the publication tracks it, added here since the publication, present in neither tree, or not a file on one side (a directory at a compared path, which an untracked directory entry produces). No branch reads a digest its state does not have.

record_format_versions.identity: the objective's source identity is newer than the objective section itself, so it is gated by the version separately: the version-4 writer recorded the objective without it and the version-2 writer recorded no objective at all, so both keep verifying, and an identity a record does carry is compared at every version
record_format_versions.piece_count: the placed-piece count is gated by the same rule because deleting it from a suite record left _summarize re-deriving a summary from episodes with no piece key and raising KeyError: 'pieces'; _summarize now omits the metric for a group that carries neither key
record_format_versions.pre_change_measurement: on the tree this repair replaces (ed8830a1), prechange_probe.py objective_identity changes the objective's clear term without touching a weight and the record verifies (exit 1 with that value); prechange_probe.py objective_required_when_versioned and suite_wide_histogram measure the version marker the previous round added on the tree that round replaced (fbe21e1)
record_format_versions.regression: objective_identity; objective_required_when_versioned; the histogram and piece-count cases in test_unit.py
record_format_versions.reused: the version numbers are reused, not a schema history: the same number was written by writers that emitted different sections, so a version says which sections the verifier must require and not which sections a record of that number happens to carry. The base commit's writer (d83a5bc, PR #9's merge) emitted the placed-piece count at version 1 for a scripted episode and at version 2 for a suite, which re-running it on experiments/000-connection, 001 and 002 reproduces below; the writer older still wrote the same numbers without that key, which is the shape the version-1 compatibility row pins. This experiment's own earlier rounds also wrote suites at version 2. A legacy version's sections may therefore be absent and are compared when present; the current version's must be present.
record_format_versions.unchanged: the weights, the agents and every recorded value are unchanged: the sections each writer emits, and the versions it emits them at, are the same as before this repair — only the objective's identity is added, and the version number the writer records moves from 4 to 5 so that the section's presence is gated

versions.1: a scripted episode; every section added since — the placed-piece count, the clear-size histogram and the declared objective — may be absent and is compared when present
versions.2: a suite; the same, with a present histogram required to be complete across the record (every episode and every agent summary), and an objective in a suite without the Tetris agent still rejected
versions.3: a scripted episode the current writer emits; it must carry pieces_placed and clear_sizes
versions.4: a suite the prior writer emitted; it must carry pieces_placed and clear_sizes on every episode, clear_sizes on every agent summary, and objective when its configuration uses the Tetris agent — every section that writer wrote, except the objective's source identity, which it never recorded
versions.5: a suite the current writer emits; it must carry all of the above, including the objective's source identity

record_format_versions.why: the verifier used to infer 'legacy record' from an absent optional section, which is the same JSON as a section deleted after the record was written: deleting `objective`, `clear_sizes` or `pieces_placed` from a newly written record left it verifying under a schema weaker than the writer's. The version is the marker that distinguishes the two cases for the versions the current writer emits.
